newsitem.title: EGYPT: Clinton and others call Mubarak on summit hitch.
newsitem.headline: Clinton and others call Mubarak on summit hitch.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton, King Hussein of Jordan, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Israeli President Ezer Weizman all called Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Sunday to try to persuade him to attend Clinton's Middle East summit in Washington on Tuesday.
Mubarak is reluctant to go until he knows what Clinton aims to achieve from the summit and what will come out of it of substance, diplomatic sources said.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat is reluctant to go unless Mubarak is there to give him moral support.

Egyptian Information Minister Safwat el-Sharif told state television about the calls and said that Mubarak's telephone conversation with Clinton dealt with "the purpose of the invitation which he (Clinton) made for a five-way summit in Washington".

"All the calls dealt with points of views on how to save the peace process and how to get out of the current crisis in a way which revives hope that the agreements signed by Israel and the Palestinian Authority will be implemented," he added.
King Hussein, who has said he will attend the summit alongside Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, made two separate calls to Mubarak, Sharif added.

The diplomatic sources said Mubarak's reluctance to go reflected Arab expectations that Clinton and Netanyahu will give them nothing but empty promises in an attempt to placate the Palestinians after four days of angry protests.
Mubarak has said Netanyahu failed to carry out the promises he made on the only occasion they have met -- in Cairo in July.
Netanyahu said on Sunday that there were no agreements in advance of the Washington summit -- a signal to Arabs that he does not intend to make any political gestures.
